title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 40 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and space.

stories.h: Space Force Taps Viasat for $450M Ops Center to Harmonize Data Network
stories.what: Space Systems Command recently awarded Viasat a contract with a $450 million ceiling to design and field a mission operations center for the command’s burgeoning Space Data Network.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: MQ-58 Valkyrie Drones Now Cost $6M-$8M Each
stories.what: Kratos still sees Valkyrie's relative affordability as key to staying ahead of a growing field of competing Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) drone designs.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: U.K. to Develop North Atlantic Network of Drones, AI Systems to Find Russian Subs
stories.what: The U.K. will invest $120 million on a network of drones, sensors and AI systems for the Royal Navy to counter Russian submarines in the North Atlantic, the Ministry of Defense announced Tuesday.
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

stories.h: Report: Russian ships are pumping tanks, MRAPs and rocket launchers into Africa
stories.what: Russian cargo ships have carried military equipment including tanks, armored vehicles and rocket launchers to African ports serving as gateways to Moscow’s forces on the continent, according to a new investigation.
stories.you: The Navy is short of ships and is turning to cheaper unmanned boats, which opens the door to new builders.

stories.h: Hegseth: Impeachment Over Policy Disagreement Sends Wrong Signal to Adversaries
stories.what: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, facing the threat of impeachment, detailed a record of successful operations on his watch during a press briefing at the Pentagon.
stories.you: Budget and policy moves decide which programs get real money and when; they're the earliest signal of demand.

watch.why: November 10. Could squeeze drone, motor and munitions supply weeks before the DoD ban.

idea.why: Low-probability-of-intercept mesh radios that keep swarms coordinated under jamming. Autonomy at scale needs links that survive. Fiber works for one drone, not a swarm.
